condition: Obstructed infected kidney (ureteric stone with sepsis)
summary: 52-year-old diabetic woman with 2 days of right loin pain then fever 39.2, rigors, BP 94/56, lactate 3.0; CT 9 mm proximal ureteric stone with hydronephrosis.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Right loin pain with fever and shaking
inputs.hpi: Type 2 diabetes. Two days of right loin pain radiating to the groin, then fever, rigors and vomiting since last night. Feels faint.

exam.general: Unwell, clammy. Pulse 122/min, BP 94/56, RR 24, temperature 39.2°C, SpO2 96%.
exam.abdomen: Right renal angle and flank tenderness, no peritonism.

imaging.name: CT KUB (low-dose, non-contrast)
imaging.result: 9 mm calculus in the right proximal ureter with moderate right hydronephrosis and perinephric fat stranding.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Obstructed infected right kidney (pyonephrosis) — 9 mm proximal ureteric stone
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Obstructed infected right kidney with sepsis: urgent decompression (nephrostomy or stent) and IV antibiotics; defer definitive stone treatment.

mustInclude.knownGapNote: Web 2026-09-25: passed before pane model 1.0.0 only because the wrong PANE top 3 (cholecystitis) seeded that protocol's tests; PANE now ranks infected obstructed kidney, which has no management protocol yet, so nothing seeds blood and urine cultures.
mustInclude.proposedFix: A protocol for the PANE node infected_obstructed_kidney (EAU Urolithiasis 2024: cultures, antibiotics, urgent decompression).

mustInclude.note: EAU: urgent decompression (nephrostomy or retrograde stent) of the obstructed infected kidney.

mustExclude.note: EAU: definitive stone removal is delayed until the infection has resolved.
The source is the obstructed kidney: decompression, not laparotomy.

guideline.name: EAU Guidelines on Urolithiasis
guideline.section: Renal colic: NSAIDs first-line analgesia (caution in reduced renal function); low-dose non-contrast CT to confirm; pregnancy: ultrasound first-line, MRI second-line, low-dose CT last resort; medical expulsive therapy (alpha-blocker) for distal ureteric stones >5 mm; obstructed infected kidney: urgent decompression (percutaneous nephrostomy or retrograde ureteral stent) with antibiotics, urine and blood cultures, definitive stone treatment delayed until infection resolved; anuria / obstructed solitary kidney: urgent decompression
guideline.citation: Skolarikos A, Jung H, Neisius A, et al. EAU Guidelines on Urolithiasis. EAU Guidelines Office, Arnhem; 2024 edition.

guideline.name: NICE NG51 — Suspected sepsis: recognition, diagnosis and early management
guideline.section: High-risk criteria (new confusion, SBP ≤90, HR >130, RR ≥25, lactate); blood cultures and broad-spectrum IV antibiotics within 1 hour for high risk; IV fluid bolus; lactate; senior review; source control
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Suspected sepsis in people aged 16 or over: recognition, assessment and early management. NICE guideline NG51 (updated 2024). London: NICE.

guideline.name: NICE NG148 — Acute kidney injury: prevention, detection and management
guideline.section: Detection (creatinine against baseline); urinalysis for all with AKI; ultrasound of the urinary tract within 24 h when obstruction is suspected (immediately if pyonephrosis suspected); stop/withhold nephrotoxic drugs (NSAIDs, ACE inhibitors, ARBs, diuretics) and review metformin; refer to urology immediately for pyonephrosis, obstructed solitary kidney, bilateral upper tract obstruction or complications of obstruction; nephrology referral criteria
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Acute kidney injury: prevention, detection and management. NICE guideline NG148. London: NICE; 2019.

rationale: The infected obstructed kidney is a urological emergency: decompress and treat sepsis, no definitive stone treatment while infected (EAU 2024).
